title: A Bridge for the Atlas
premise: In 1899, Kestrel Dunmore, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Atlas Trading Company, has spent his life believing that history is something that happens in capitals, not in his fog-bound harbor town. When the colonial army requisitions the town for a war nobody asked for and seizes the company ledger containing every indentured name, Kestrel's careful invisibility shatters: the ledger decides who is evacuated, who is conscripted, and who is left behind. To save his family he must steal back the one book that owns them all, forging names and alliances at the cost of betraying the friend who taught him to read. In the end, with only one berth on the last ship before the century turns, Kestrel gives it to his sister, stays behind to carry the town's memory himself, and discovers that survival is not the same as living.
about_author: H. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping ledgers before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary people are recorded, erased, and remembered by institutions that never learned their faces.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel dives the shallows at dawn while his sister Briony mends nets, establishing the family's fragile economy under Atlas Company debt. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet pride in skill, shadowed by the knowledge that everything they own belongs to someone else.

chapters.title: Names in a Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel delivers pearls to the company house and glimpses the great ledger where every diver's debt is inked. The clerk's son, Tobias, secretly teaches him letters using ledger entries. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease as he sees his own name reduced to a sum.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Horizon
chapters.summary: A warship appears off the coast; rumor says the army will requisition the town as a supply port. Father Dunmore dismisses it—history doesn't come here. POV: Briony. Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding, the calm before institutional violence.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers occupy the company house and seize all records, including the ledger of names. Indentured families are ordered to register or be treated as runaways. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering that paperwork, not soldiers, holds real power over their lives.

chapters.title: What the Army Wants
chapters.summary: Captain Verrin announces able-bodied men will be conscripted as divers and laborers for a blockade operation. Father is taken for processing. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness; the first crack in his belief that obedience ensures safety.

chapters.title: Tobias's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tobias reveals the army trusts him with ledger copies and offers to alter Kestrel's entry—if Kestrel helps him smuggle out evidence of the captain's graft. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: friendship tested by risk; both boys realize they've stopped being children.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: By lamplight they amend the copy: Kestrel marked 'deceased,' freeing him from conscription. Guilt surfaces—he is safe only by erasing himself. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the intoxication and shame of becoming someone the record says does not exist.

chapters.title: Briony's Discovery
chapters.summary: Briony finds the forged page and confronts Kestrel: if he's dead on paper, who pays the family debt? She proposes taking the risk herself instead. POV: Briony. Emotional beat: sibling love expressed as argument; the price of survival becomes literal arithmetic.

chapters.title: Father Returns
chapters.summary: Father comes back broken from the diving conscription, lungs damaged, unable to work the deep beds. The debt now falls entirely on the children. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief for a parent still alive; the slow corruption of a man who once taught pride in the work.

chapters.title: Verrin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel copies proof of Verrin's graft—sold supplies, phantom workers—but hesitates to hand it over, realizing Tobias could hang for theft. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: moral paralysis; power corrupts even those who only hold its shadow.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Soldiers raid the divers' quarter hunting a runaway; a neighbor with no papers is dragged away and never returns. Briony burns her own registration rather than be listed. POV: Briony. Emotional beat: terror hardening into defiance; memory becomes an act of resistance.

chapters.title: A Ship Is Chartered
chapters.summary: News spreads: one evacuation ship before the century turns, berths assigned strictly by ledger status. Families turn on each other, bribing and denouncing. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: community dissolving; the revelation that scarcity, not cruelty, is the engine of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: Tobias admits he already gave Verrin the original amended pages to protect his father's job—the forgery exists only in Kestrel's memory now. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: betrayal without malice; the devastating discovery that institutions make liars of everyone.

chapters.title: Dead Man Diving
chapters.summary: Kestrel works the deep beds illegally as an unregistered man, earning berth money no ledger can trace. A near-drowning forces him to admit he cannot buy three berths. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grim competence masking despair; the arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Verrin's Offer
chapters.summary: Captain Verrin, suspecting the forgery, offers Kestrel two berths in exchange for naming whoever altered the ledger. He suspects Tobias. POV: Verrin. Emotional beat: cold temptation; power revealed as a machine that runs on other people's loyalty.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Kestrel weighs giving up Tobias against saving both parents, then learns Father's lungs will fail within the year regardless—one berth, not two. He must choose which family member leaves. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the novel's moral climax compressed into a single sleepless night.

chapters.title: Fire in the Records House
chapters.summary: Kestrel burns the requisition annex, destroying the army's claim on every unregistered diver—including himself—and frames nothing, claiming the act openly to shield Tobias. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction; he finally makes history happen here.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: On the dock, Kestrel puts Briony aboard with their mother's ring and the memorized names of every diver in the ledger. Father refuses to leave his bed; Kestrel stays. POV: Briony. Emotional beat: farewell as inheritance; grief and gratitude indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Century's Turn
chapters.summary: New Year's Eve under occupation: Verrin, exposed by Tobias's surviving copies, is recalled in disgrace but unpunished. Kestrel tends his father through the night as the year dies. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: bitter catharsis; justice partial, survival incomplete.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Spring: Father dies quietly. Kestrel dives one last time and leaves the pearls on the seabed, refusing the company's economy forever. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into refusal; the sea as the only honest ledger.

chapters.title: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Kestrel begins teaching the harbor children their letters, writing the town's true history from memory on salvaged slate—building, name by name, a bridge across the century. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: purpose found in witness; memory as the antidote to ledgers.

chapters.title: Letters from Across the Water
chapters.summary: Years later, Briony's letters arrive with money and news; Kestrel reads them aloud to his students, including one line: 'You were never invisible to me.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: resolution without restoration; the price was paid, and the remembering has just begun.
